chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a garment in which a man becomes junub and sweats in it. He said: “As for me, I do not like to sleep in it; but if it is winter, then there is no harm, so long as he has not sweated in it.”

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or clothing being discussed
key_terms.الشِّتَاءُ: winter, mentioned as a relevant condition in the ruling
key_terms.لَا أُحِبُّ: I do not like; indicates dislike rather than absolute prohibition
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: to enter the state of janabah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sleeping in a garment worn during janabah if one has sweated in it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on a garment worn while a person is in janabah, especially when sweat is involved. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states his dislike of sleeping in such a garment, while indicating there is no harm in winter if no sweating has occurred.
